title: Cube
text:
A Bebras cube has a different shape on each face. The six shapes are shown below. 

Pink circle	Purple diamond	Red ellipse	Blue pentagon	Orange star	Green triangle
					


Eight identical Bebras cubes are stacked together to form a larger cube. 



Question
In a single Bebras cube, which shape is on the face opposite the pink circle?

title: Chung cake
text:
In Vietnam, people celebrate the Lunar New Year by eating BanhChung. These rice cakes are too sticky to cut with a knife, so pieces of string are used to make the cuts:

Multiple strings can be used to cut a cake but they may get tangled if not used in the correct order. For example, in the case below, the cake should be cut using the light coloured string first, followed by the dark coloured string. If done in reverse, the dark coloured string will get tangled with the light coloured string.

Question
In what order should the four strings be used so no string gets tangled with another?

title: Treasure hunt
text:
Beavers have hidden some treasure on their secret island. They have left an encoded message revealing the location of the treasure.

They also left some clues to help decode the message:

Task
Using the clues, decode the message to reveal where we should look for the treasure.

title: Planes
text:

The planes' take-off schedule is shown below.

Task
Fill in the empty boxes in the timetable by dragging and dropping these 4 planes.

title: Fair
text:
At the fair, beavers wearing funny hats enjoy themselves by walking about on stilts. Each beaver chooses stilts so that the tops of their hats are all at the same height.

Question 
Move the beavers to stilts by dragging them so that they are all the same height.

title: Parking at the party
text:
Ana invites friends to her house every week. They arrive by car. In Ana’s driveway there is space for 9 cars, but they need to park in 3 lanes of 3 cars. Each friend is asked to park as far forward as possible in any lane to make room for other cars.

Last week (picture above), car A arrived first, then car D, then car C, and then cars B, E, and F. The cars parked this way (not blocking car C) because car C needed to leave first.

This week, friends arrive in this order:

Ann, Bob, Claire, David, Elen, Frank, George, Hailey, Ivan

They will leave the party in this order:

George, David, Frank, Ivan, Hailey, Claire, Bob, Ann,  Elen

Question
Which way can the friends park as they arrive so that no car is blocked in when its owner tries to leave?

title: Avoiding the clouds
text:
A pilot flying to a nearby airport encounters some stormy clouds. They want to avoid these clouds and fly through clear sky.  

The section of the cloudy sky is represented as a 3x3x3 grid. As the pilot moves one step forward, she can also turn the plane to move up, down, left, right, or diagonally. The plane cannot move out of the grid. 

In the diagram the white clouds are nearest (layer 1), the light grey clouds are further away (layer 2), and the darkest clouds are furthest (layer 3).

The plane is about to enter the cloudy area. Unless it turns, it will go into the white cloud in the middle of the top row.

Question
Which instructions will move the plane through the cloudy area without flying into any clouds?

title: Rubber rings
text:
In a water park, rubber rings float downstream () along a short lazy river. At the end of the river, they line up as shown in the image below.





Children take a ring to use for their next ride from any position. When a ring is pulled out () of the water for someone's next ride, each ring behind it floats one position () downstream to fill the gap.

In our example above, where F and A are pulled out, the number of times a ring floats down by one position downstream is 8 (G and H move when F is removed; all of the remaining rings move when A is removed).

Question
Eight rings line up as shown below. Then 5 rings are pulled out of the water in the order B, G, E, D, H. In total, how many times do the rings float one position downstream?

title: Island research expeditions
text:
A research team needs to investigate all the islands in a region. 

The research team cannot investigate all islands in a single research trip.

During a single research trip, the team: 

Flies by helicopter to 1 island
Can take a ferry in the direction of the arrows to visit other islands,
Leave from the same island where they originally landed, to rejoin the helicopter.



What is the minimum number of different research trips the team must make to ensure that every island is visited at least once?

title: Tree records
text:
Emil and his friends love to hike. During their hikes, Emil's friends collect information about different aspects of trees they discover, and they record the facts on record sheets.

	Severin collects information on leaf shapes ( ). He records the shape and the corresponding tree species ().

	Quirina collects information about fruit (). She records the type of fruit and the corresponding tree species (). She also records whether the tree is a conifer ().

	Ladina collects information about the bark. She records the colour () and whether it is a good timber to construct beaver lodges () as well as the corresponding tree species ().
 
Emil has found a leaf in the forest and can see its shape. He wants to know whether the bark of this tree is suitable for making a beaver lodge. 
 
Question
Which of his friends does he have to ask, and in which order, to find the right answer?

title: Incorrect sequence
text:
Xavier is programming his first app and is writing code to transform a picture. At first, he programs only two operations: 

M (Mirror) reverses the image along the vertical axis
R (Rotate) turns the image 90° clockwise 
Input	Operation	Output
	Mirror	
	Rotate	

You can transform this original picture into this final picture with several different command sequences. 

Question
Which sequence of operations does not transform the original picture into the final picture?

title: Seoul City Tour
text:
Seoul provides tour buses for tourists. The tour buses connect Seoul's major tourist attractions. The figure shows the main attractions. The stars indicate how popular the attractions are. The lines indicate the bus connections. Each line indicates how long the connection is in kilometers.

When visiting the locations, you can collect the number of traveller stars in your travel book.

Question 

After visiting the Royal Palace,  Susie wants to take a tour bus, but she has a transport card that only allows her to travel up to 10 kilometres.  Design a route to visit attractions so that she can collect as many traveller stars as possible. Each attraction can be visited only once.

Click a connection to select it. The counter in the top right corner shows the total distance in kilometers of the selected connections. Click "Cancel answer" to delete your entries. When you're finished, click "Save answer."

title: Exciting water slide
text:
The Beaver Amusement Park has an exciting waterslide. The following diagrams show how it works: a mechanism controls the exit direction at each fork. Whenever a beaver passes through a fork, the mechanism flips, changing the exit direction.

Dan wants to try the waterslide. His mother wants to know where Dan will exit the slide so that she can position herself to take good pictures. She first sees a beaver exit from slide B, and then another from slide C. There is one more beaver waiting in line before Dan.

Question 
Which slide will Dan exit from? Click on the letter of the slide, then save.
